name: Review new investments and mandates for risk (independent risk opinion)
summary: Before the investment committee decides on a direct investment, co-investment, fund commitment, private loan or new external mandate, the investment risk oversight team writes an independent risk opinion that goes into the committee paper. A risk manager reads the memo and model, questions the deal team, checks concentration, currency, leverage and liquidity against limits and client policies, has portfolio risk model the investment's contribution to each client's risk, runs downside scenarios and drafts the opinion, which the director and, for larger items, the chief risk officer review. The review is squeezed between the deal team's memo and the committee paper deadline, waits on answers from busy deal teams, and is redone when terms change late.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian provincial public-sector asset manager with about $79 billion for four client institutions, a growing private markets program and a five-person investment risk oversight team.
baseline.notes: Snapshot at the end of 2021: about 35 direct and co-investment transactions a year, new fund commitments and manager searches; Investment Department Committees introduced in 2021 below the Management Investment Committee.

trigger: A deal team sends a draft investment memo, or a request for review with a target committee date, for a direct investment, co-investment, fund commitment, private loan or new mandate.
end_state: The director-approved (and, where needed, CRO-reviewed) independent risk opinion is filed in the committee paper, updated for any late term change; or the deal is withdrawn before the opinion is written.

volume.seasonality: Deal flow is lumpy and clusters before committee dates and quarter ends; activity was lower in spring 2020 and rose in 2021.

evidence.note: Eight private equity direct and co-investment deals closed in 2021 among about 35 transactions; volume equals committee submissions per the organisation file (mode 8 a month).

steps.name: Log the review request and confirm the committee date
steps.description: A manager in investment risk oversight records the request from a deal team in the review tracker with the asset class, size, owning client portfolios and target committee date, and asks for the draft memo, model and data room access.

error.defect_description: The committee date or owning portfolios are logged wrongly.

evidence.note: Investment risk support facilitates transaction reviews for the investment teams. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pre-committee risk reviews was found.

steps.name: Assign a reviewer and set the review depth
steps.description: The director of investment risk oversight assigns a reviewer and decides on a full review for new direct deals, co-investments, new strategies and large commitments, or a short-form review for re-ups with existing partners, small follow-ons and mandate resizing.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

evidence.note: Independent review of new strategies and products (VOLTS) and expanded independent assessment of higher risk direct private transactions (plan). Shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Read the memo, model and due diligence reports
steps.description: The reviewer reads the draft memo and the deal team's model and skims the key diligence reports (financial, technical, legal summary, operational due diligence on the manager or partner), noting assumptions, leverage terms, currency, exit and liquidity features and questions.

error.defect_description: A material term in the model or diligence reports is overlooked.

evidence.note: Risk review of private market transactions at Ontario public plans; stress testing built into due diligence. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pre-committee risk reviews was found.

steps.name: Send questions and data requests to the deal team
steps.description: The reviewer emails the deal team a list of questions and requests: sensitivities, debt terms and covenants, hedging plans, look-through exposures, key person terms and how the investment is split across client portfolios.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

next.condition: private credit deal, fund or credit mandate

evidence.note: Shares follow the process map's triggers: co-investments, direct real asset deals, private credit, fund commitments and manager searches. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pre-committee risk reviews was found.

steps.name: Private equity deal team answers the risk team's questions
steps.description: A senior member of the private equity deal team answers the question list, sends the latest model and sponsor materials, explains assumptions the risk manager queried and says which points the memo will address. Some deals drop out at this stage because a seller picks another bidder or diligence finds a problem.

error.defect_description: An answer is incomplete or based on an outdated model version.

evidence.note: Investment risk support works closely with investment teams on transaction reviews; reviews need the strategy's liquidity, leverage and complexity details. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pre-committee risk reviews was found.

steps.name: Assess concentration and currency against limits and risk budgets
steps.description: The reviewer adds the investment to current holdings by owning client portfolio and checks exposure to the single asset, sponsor or manager, sector, country and vintage against board limits, client policy constraints and the asset class risk budget, and looks at the currency exposure and planned hedging.

error.defect_description: A look-through exposure to the same sponsor or asset is missed.

control.basis: Pension Benefits Standards Regulations, 1985, Schedule III: the 10 per cent limit on investing in one person and the 30 per cent voting share limit for pension plan clients, plus each client's statement of investment policies

evidence.note: Quantitative limits from Schedule III; acceptable risk ranges and internal ratings for alternative assets per FSRA. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pre-committee risk reviews was found.

steps.name: Analyse leverage, refinancing and liquidity impact
steps.description: The reviewer reviews the debt package and covenants, refinancing dates and interest rate hedging, and estimates the investment's effect on each client's liquidity coverage, including unfunded commitments and capital calls, using the latest liquidity forecast.

error.defect_description: Unfunded commitments are left out of the liquidity impact.

evidence.note: Liquidity coverage ratio including capital calls; liquidity of positions assessed at origination per VOLTS. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pre-committee risk reviews was found.

steps.name: Model the investment's contribution to client portfolio risk
steps.description: An analyst in portfolio risk maps the investment to a proxy in the risk system and calculates its marginal contribution to total and active risk for each owning client portfolio and the change in factor exposures.

error.defect_description: The proxy chosen understates the asset's risk.

evidence.note: Asset class risks tied to common factors in the model manager's risk system; marginal risk of individual assets per FSRA. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pre-committee risk reviews was found.

steps.name: Run downside and stress scenarios on the deal model
steps.description: The reviewer runs downside cases on the deal model and the portfolio, such as higher rates and refinancing costs, lower exit multiples, a revenue or occupancy shock and currency moves, separately and together, and notes the loss and covenant headroom in each.

error.defect_description: A stress case is applied to the wrong base case.

evidence.note: Stress testing incorporated into due diligence before an alternative investment (FSRA); risk review to include stress tests (VOLTS). Times are author estimates; no published time study of pre-committee risk reviews was found.

steps.name: Assess partner, key person, counterparty and structural risks
steps.description: The reviewer weighs the sponsor or manager track record and alignment, key person and governance terms, counterparty and structural risks, and how the investment fits the risk appetite, and decides whether there are concerns to raise before writing.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

evidence.note: Risk review covers complexity, liquidity and adequacy of skills (VOLTS); peer private markets risk reviews. Shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Discuss concerns and mitigants with the deal team
steps.description: The reviewer meets the deal team to discuss the concerns, for example sizing, hedging, leverage or conditions, and records the mitigants the team accepts; where the structure or size changes the stress cases are rerun.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

evidence.note: Common practice; deal teams revise memos after risk comments, as the upstream workflows model. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pre-committee risk reviews was found.

steps.name: Draft the independent risk opinion
steps.description: The reviewer writes the two to four page opinion for the committee paper: summary view and risk rating, key risks and mitigants, concentration, leverage, liquidity and stress results, fit with the risk budget and any recommended conditions.

error.defect_description: The opinion misstates a term or a limit number.

control.basis: Second-line independent risk opinion required in investment committee papers under the investment approval policy; risk function separate from investment teams (three lines model observed by FSRA)

evidence.note: Independent risk perspective on investment decisions (The model manager); separate risk control team (FSRA); independent review at origination (VOLTS). Times are author estimates; no published time study of pre-committee risk reviews was found.

steps.name: Director reviews and challenges the risk opinion
steps.description: The director of investment risk oversight reads the opinion against the memo, challenges the rating and conditions, checks consistency with past opinions and either approves it, asks for changes or routes it to the chief risk officer for items going to the Management Investment Committee or the board.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

control.basis: Investment risk oversight review standard: director sign-off of every risk opinion before submission

evidence.note: Investment Department Committees approve up to set thresholds; larger items go to the Management Investment Committee co-chaired by the CRO. Shares and waits are author estimates.

steps.name: Chief risk officer reviews the opinion for a senior committee item
steps.description: For investments going to the Management Investment Committee, which the chief risk officer co-chairs, or to the board, the CRO reads the opinion and memo and either agrees or asks for a stronger or different view.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

control.basis: Management Investment Committee mandate: CIO and CRO co-chair and every item needing board approval is first recommended by the committee

evidence.note: Management Investment Committee composition and role. Waits are author estimates.

steps.name: Prepare a short-form risk opinion
steps.description: For a re-up with an existing partner, a small follow-on or a mandate resize, the reviewer checks the changes since the last review, updates concentration and liquidity figures and writes a one-page opinion.

error.defect_description: A change since the last review is missed.

evidence.note: Tiered review depth is common practice. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pre-committee risk reviews was found.

steps.name: Send the final opinion for factual check and to the committee secretariat
steps.description: The reviewer sends the approved opinion to the deal team to check facts, makes any factual corrections and files it with the investment office for the committee paper.

error.defect_description: A superseded draft is filed.

evidence.note: Common practice. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pre-committee risk reviews was found.

steps.name: Insert the opinion into the committee paper and log it
steps.description: The investment office adds the risk opinion to the committee paper behind the memo, records it in the committee tracker and circulates the paper by the deadline.

error.defect_description: The opinion is attached to the wrong paper version.

evidence.note: Formal committee mandates set out the approval and review process. Waits are author estimates.

steps.name: Update the opinion for late changes to terms
steps.description: When price, leverage, size or the client split changes after the paper is circulated, the reviewer updates the affected analysis, writes an addendum or revised opinion and gets the director's agreement by email.

error.defect_description: An affected figure is not updated.

evidence.note: Late term changes are common in competitive deals. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pre-committee risk reviews was found.

exceptions.name: Short-form review
exceptions.description: Re-ups with existing partners, small follow-ons and mandate resizes get a one-page opinion without the full analysis.

exceptions.name: Deal withdrawn during the review
exceptions.description: The seller picks another bidder, exclusivity lapses or diligence finds a problem and the deal team drops the deal before the opinion is written.

exceptions.name: Concerns lead to a restructured deal
exceptions.description: The risk manager's concerns change the size, leverage or hedging, and the stress cases are rerun before the opinion is written.

exceptions.name: Senior committee item
exceptions.description: Investments above Investment Department Committee authority need the chief risk officer's review before the Management Investment Committee or the board.

exceptions.name: Late change to terms
exceptions.description: Price, leverage, size or client split changes after the paper is circulated and the opinion is updated with an addendum.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the review request to the opinion filed in the committee paper
benchmarks.population: Independent risk reviews at a Canadian public-sector asset manager, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author estimate: the upstream fund commitment and manager search workflows allow two to seven days (mode four) plus a day of hands-on time for the risk opinion before the paper goes to committee; full reviews of direct deals run longer and short-form reviews shorter.

pain_points.description: Seller and committee deadlines leave little time for the review; the risk team often starts before the memo is final and must redo work when terms change late.

evidence.note: Author estimate; tight deal timelines are named in the organisation file's process description.

pain_points.description: Answers from deal teams busy with diligence and negotiation are slow, and some deals drop out after the risk team has started.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

pain_points.description: Private assets have no market prices, so their contribution to portfolio risk rests on proxies that can understate risk; the risk system then in use gave limited insight into tail risks.
Strategies with non-linear or tail risk can look harmless on value at risk; reviews need stress tests, liquidity and complexity checks at origination, which take senior time.
Concentration has to be checked by client portfolio because each client has its own policy and legal limits, done in spreadsheets from several systems.

assumptions: One case is one risk opinion for one committee submission. The deal team's diligence, memo drafting and memo revisions after the opinion are counted in the upstream workflows (fund commitment, manager search and the direct deal processes); only the deal team's time answering risk questions is counted here, split across the five teams in proportion to the process map's triggers.

Handoff timing: the upstream fund commitment and manager search workflows model the risk opinion as one step with a two to seven day wait and four to fifteen hours of work. This workflow details that step; it runs longer for full reviews of direct deals because it includes waits on deal team answers and the portfolio risk analyst, and the review often starts while the memo is still being finished. The simulated median (about 9 days) is above the 7-day estimate because full reviews of direct deals make up most cases.

Schedule III of the federal Pension Benefits Standards Regulations is cited for the 10 per cent and 30 per cent limits; it applies to Ontario pension plans through Ontario's pension regulation (author's knowledge, not opened). It binds the pension plan clients, not the insurance client insurance fund, whose own policy sets its limits.

Review depth, shares of short-form reviews, senior committee items and late term changes are author estimates. The 2021 introduction of Investment Department Committees below the Management Investment Committee is from the annual report.
The portfolio risk analyst and the investment office manager take part although the process map lists only the two investment risk oversight roles; both roles exist in the organisation file.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file; investment professionals are priced from estimated total pay.

Staffing: about 1.35 FTE stated (1.0 investment risk manager); hands-on time times volume implies a similar figure. The rest of the four managers' time goes to counterparty exposure monitoring, valuation challenge and portfolio-level private markets risk work.
Times, waits and branch probabilities are author estimates (tier C) because no published time study of pre-committee risk reviews was found.
